subject: Quick question: per-1M token pricing & model list
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@byteforge.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick question: per-1M token pricing & model list

Hi Olga,

We're evaluating hosted inference providers for a Q1 2027 pilot and I wanted a concise cost baseline before scheduling a technical call. Can you send your current standard per-1M token rates (separated by input/output where applicable) and a short model matrix showing available hosted models (base/finetuned, typical latency tier, and any quantized variants)?

A couple of context points:
- Pilot expected to be ~50M tokens/month initially (mixed input/output)
- Low-latency chat use cases are higher priority than cheapest throughput
- We may ask for pricing bands if the pilot scales quickly to 200M+/mo

If you have a one-page cost sheet + model catalog CSV that'd be perfect. Thanks — looking for something I can forward to procurement.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Lee
Head of ML Platforms | ByteForge.ai
aaron.lee@byteforge.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@byteforge.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick question: per-1M token pricing & model list

Hi Aaron — great to hear from you and thanks for the context.

Attaching our current hosted API rate sheet and a compact model catalog (CSV) — the sheet shows per-1M token input/output rates, plus our recommended model families for low-latency vs throughput. High-level:
- Small/fast family (quantized): $0.60 / $0.75 per 1M (input / output)
- General-purpose family: $1.20 / $1.50 per 1M
- High-capability family (larger context/LLM): $3.50 / $4.00 per 1M

Those are standard published tiers; we routinely offer committed-volume discounts and a first-quarter pilot allowance for evaluation. I copied pricing in the attached PDF and included a boolean column in the CSV for quantized variants.

Next step: If that looks aligned, want to loop in our sales lead to talk pilot-term discounts and a simple mutual action plan? I can also provide an estimated cost model for your 50M/mo profile.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
(650) 555-0224

Attachments: redwood_hosted_ratecard_v2026-11.pdf (PDF, 1 page), model_catalog_2026-11.csv (CSV, 1 page)

From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@byteforge.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick question: per-1M token pricing & model list

Thanks Olga — received and appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple follow-ups from procurement:

1) Do you publish separate input vs output billing in the invoice or is that aggregated? Procurement prefers separate line items.
2) For the 50M/month pilot, what uplift/discount would you typically offer on the general-purpose family? We were thinking a committed 3-month pilot with the option to convert to a 12-month seat/commit.
3) Any minimums or required commitments to access lower-priced quantized options?

Can you also confirm whether you have a preferred contract template (we usually start from our standard SOW + MSLA) or whether Redwood prefers to use its own? I'll share that with procurement if needed.

On the technical side, our SRE will want to confirm latency targets — can your model catalog include typical p95 generation latencies for 512-token responses on a dedicated host?

— Aaron

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick question: per-1M token pricing & model list

Ben / Marissa — looping you both in for pricing and procurement coordination on the ByteForge pilot (see thread below). Key asks: separate input/output line items, three-month pilot (50M/mo) with option to convert to annual commit, and p95 latency numbers for 512-token responses on dedicated hosts.

My suggested quick offer:
- Pilot (3 months, 50M/mo): apply a 15% pilot discount off published general-purpose family rates; provide an allowance of one-week of burst capacity for initial load testing.
- Annual conversion: if they convert to a 12-month committed spend >= 200M/mo equivalent, move to tiered pricing (25% discount on general-purpose, 35% on quantized small/fast family).

Questions for you: are these discount bands workable from a commercial perspective? Also, procurement asked about invoicing format — we should confirm we can produce separate input/output line items. I've attached the published ratecard PDF and model catalog CSV for reference.

Thanks — Olga

Subject: Re: Quick question: per-1M token pricing & model list

Hi Aaron — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers inline, plus a pilot offer below.

1) Invoice line items: we can produce separate invoice line items for input and output token volumes — procurement-friendly.

2) Pilot discount: for a 3-month committed pilot at 50M/mo on the general-purpose family we can offer a 15% pilot discount (applied to both input & output lines). Example cost estimate attached.

3) Quantized options: quantized small/fast family is available without additional minimums on hosted; access to the lowest latency capacity is subject to capacity windows during a pilot but not locked behind long-term commitments.

Pilot offer summary (3 months):
- Hosted general-purpose (standard): published $1.20 / $1.50 per 1M (input/output)
- Pilot rate (15% off): $1.02 / $1.275 per 1M
- 50M/mo profile estimate (monthly): Input tokens cost = $1.02 * (estimated input portion) — I'll send a quick cost model once you confirm the input/output split (if you don't have one we can assume 40% input / 60% output as a starting point).
- Onboarding: 2 weeks of implementation support + 1 week of burst testing included

Next steps: If that sounds reasonable I can: (a) share a short 1-page commercial memo for your procurement, (b) schedule a 30-min call with Ben for contract terms, and (c) have our SRE share p95 latency numbers for 512-token responses on dedicated hosts (we'll send a short latency table).

Would Tuesday or Wednesday next week work for the short call?

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
